messages:
Jenna: FYI ACME is blocked on the POC — their test calls are returning 401/403. customer pasted the payload below. Can we triage?

Priya: thanks, passing to eng. can you paste the exact error body + request-id header if available?

Jenna: error body: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key provided"}`
response headers included `x-request-id: 8a7f3c2b`. they said sometimes they get `403 Forbidden` with `org/project mismatch` in the logs.

Marco: quick checklist — did they create a key under the right org and project? common issue: keys are scoped to org, and you need X-Redwood-Org header or the key must belong to that org.

Priya: can you confirm the curl they ran? often the header is missing or the key is from a different workspace.

Jenna: they ran: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'```
no X-Redwood-Org header.

Alex: that explains the 401 for a key that exists but isn't matched to a default org in our lookup. If no X-Redwood-Org header, we try to infer org from key metadata — but if the key was created under a different enterprise org (org mismatch), you'll see `403 org/project mismatch` downstream.

Morgan: quick mitigation for the POC: ask the customer to add `-H "X-Redwood-Org: acme-poc"` to their request (replace with the org slug they used to generate the key). Also verify the API key's last 6 chars so we can look it up in logs (ask them to share only last 6).

Jenna: shared with customer: please confirm your org slug and the last 6 chars of the key. Customer replied: org `acme-poc`, key ends with `9f4b2c`.

Alex: searching logs for x-request-id 8a7f3c2b and key suffix 9f4b2c... found entries: `2026-02-12T17:12:03Z request_id=8a7f3c2b auth_status=key_found org=acme-prod requested_org=acme-poc result=forbidden org_mismatch`. So the key is registered under `acme-prod` but they are calling with `X-Redwood-Org: acme-poc` (or vice-versa). This is the mismatch.

Priya: options for customer: 1) create a new key under `acme-poc` and use that, or 2) we can add a temporary mapping if they need `acme-prod` key to work for a short POC window (requires enterprise consent). Which do they prefer?

Jenna: they want fastest path — create new key under acme-poc. they asked if any scope is required for generate/chat.

Morgan: keys should have `model:invoke` scope (default for API keys from the Console). If they used a restricted key that lacks `model:invoke` you'll see 403 and an error like `insufficient_scopes`. Also check project-level access: if the key is project-scoped, ensure the project id in the request (if they set one) matches.

Marco: I'll paste a minimal curl they can use to verify after they create a new key: ```curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED_NEW" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Org: acme-poc" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gptx-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'```
If they still get 401, ask for the `x-request-id` and the exact `Date` header from the response so we can correlate.

Priya: also watch for proxy/infra rewriting Authorization header — some corporate proxies will strip `Authorization` by default. if they have an ingress that terminates TLS and forwards, header could be lost.

Alex: I've temporarily added an audit entry to allow lookup by key suffix 9f4b2c so we can validate once they try new key. No code changes needed. If they want the mapping route, that needs contract approval.

Jenna: customer created a new key and tried the curl above; they report back: `200 OK` and returned token streaming. POC unblocked.

Priya: awesome. can we capture this in the ticket with recommended troubleshooting steps so AE can reuse?

Morgan: I'll add a short KB to the POC playbook: "Auth failures during POC" — include checks: key org ownership, X-Redwood-Org header, key scopes, project id mismatch, proxy header stripping, request-id logging.

Marco: tagging @eng-runtime for visibility in case we want a better error message that suggests `org mismatch` and includes the expected org slug in the response (obv don't leak orgs in public errors, but for enterprise-only responses we could be clearer).

eng-runtime-bot: Incident detector — no service incident. Logged support activity: S-1234 (ACME POC auth triage).

Jenna: thanks everyone — closing this swarm. :thumbsup:
